segs.p: Majjhima Nikāya 106
segs.e: Middle Discourses 106

segs.p: Āneñjasappāyasutta
segs.e: Conducive to the Imperturbable

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kurūsu viharati kammāsadhammaṁ nāma kurūnaṁ nigamo.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kurus, near the Kuru town named Kammāsadamma.

segs.p: Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

segs.p: “bhikkhavo”ti.
segs.e: “Mendicants!”

segs.p: “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Venerable sir,” they replied.

segs.p: Bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Aniccā, bhikkhave, kāmā tucchā musā mosadhammā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, sensual pleasures are impermanent, hollow, false, and deceptive.

segs.p: Māyākatametaṁ, bhikkhave, bālalāpanaṁ.
segs.e: This is made by illusion, mendicants, lamented by fools.

segs.p: Ye ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmā, ye ca samparāyikā kāmā;
segs.e: Sensual pleasures in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: yā ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmasaññā, yā ca samparāyikā kāmasaññā—
segs.e: sensual perceptions in this life and in lives to come;

segs.p: ubhayametaṁ māradheyyaṁ, mārassesa visayo, mārassesa nivāpo, mārassesa gocaro.
segs.e: both of these are Māra’s dominion, Māra’s domain, Māra’s lair, and Māra’s range.

segs.p: Etthete pāpakā akusalā mānasā abhijjhāpi byāpādāpi sārambhāpi saṁvattanti.
segs.e: They conduce to bad, unskillful notions such as desire, ill will, and aggression.

segs.p: Teva ariyasāvakassa idhamanusikkhato antarāyāya sambhavanti.
segs.e: And they create an obstacle for a noble disciple training here.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: A noble disciple reflects on this:

segs.p: ‘ye ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmā, ye ca samparāyikā kāmā;
segs.e: ‘Sensual pleasures in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: yā ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmasaññā, yā ca samparāyikā kāmasaññā—
segs.e: sensual perceptions in this life and in lives to come;

segs.p: ubhayametaṁ māradheyyaṁ, mārassesa visayo, mārassesa nivāpo, mārassesa gocaro.
segs.e: both of these are Māra’s dominion, Māra’s domain, Māra’s lair, and Māra’s range.

segs.p: Etthete pāpakā akusalā mānasā abhijjhāpi byāpādāpi sārambhāpi saṁvattanti,
segs.e: They conduce to bad, unskillful notions such as desire, ill will, and aggression.

segs.p: teva ariyasāvakassa idhamanusikkhato antarāyāya sambhavanti.
segs.e: And they create an obstacle for a noble disciple training here.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ vipulena mahaggatena cetasā vihareyyaṁ abhibhuyya lokaṁ adhiṭṭhāya manasā.
segs.e: Why don’t I meditate with an abundant, expansive heart, having mastered the world and stabilized the mind?

segs.p: Vipulena hi me mahaggatena cetasā viharato abhibhuyya lokaṁ adhiṭṭhāya manasā ye pāpakā akusalā mānasā abhijjhāpi byāpādāpi sārambhāpi te na bhavissanti.
segs.e: Then I will have no more bad, unskillful notions such as desire, ill will, and aggression.

segs.p: Tesaṁ pahānā aparittañca me cittaṁ bhavissati appamāṇaṁ subhāvitan’ti.
segs.e: And by giving them up my mind, no longer limited, will become limitless and well developed.’

segs.p: Tassa evaṁpaṭipannassa tabbahulavihārino āyatane cittaṁ pasīdati.
segs.e: Practicing in this way and meditating on it often their mind becomes confident in this dimension.

segs.p: Sampasāde sati etarahi vā āneñjaṁ samāpajjati paññāya vā adhimuccati.
segs.e: Being confident, they either attain the imperturbable now, or are freed by wisdom.

segs.p: Kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā, ṭhānametaṁ vijjati yaṁ taṁsaṁvattanikaṁ viññāṇaṁ assa āneñjūpagaṁ.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, it’s possible that that conducive consciousness will be reborn in the imperturbable.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamā āneñjasappāyā paṭipadā akkhāyati.
segs.e: This is said to be the first way of practice suitable for attaining the imperturbable.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘ye ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmā, ye ca samparāyikā kāmā;
segs.e: ‘Sensual pleasures in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: yā ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmasaññā, yā ca samparāyikā kāmasaññā;
segs.e: sensual perceptions in this life and in lives to come;

segs.p: yaṁ kiñci rūpaṁ sabbaṁ rūpaṁ cattāri ca mahābhūtāni, catunnañca mahābhūtānaṁ upādāyarūpan’ti.
segs.e: whatever form there is, all form is the four principal states, or form derived from the four principal states.’

segs.p: Tassa evaṁpaṭipannassa tabbahulavihārino āyatane cittaṁ pasīdati.
segs.e: Practicing in this way and meditating on it often their mind becomes confident in this dimension.

segs.p: Sampasāde sati etarahi vā āneñjaṁ samāpajjati paññāya vā adhimuccati.
segs.e: Being confident, they either attain the imperturbable now, or are freed by wisdom.

segs.p: Kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā, ṭhānametaṁ vijjati yaṁ taṁsaṁvattanikaṁ viññāṇaṁ assa āneñjūpagaṁ.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, it’s possible that that conducive consciousness will be reborn in the imperturbable.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyā āneñjasappāyā paṭipadā akkhāyati.
segs.e: This is said to be the second way of practice suitable for attaining the imperturbable.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘ye ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmā, ye ca samparāyikā kāmā;
segs.e: ‘Sensual pleasures in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: yā ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmasaññā, yā ca samparāyikā kāmasaññā;
segs.e: sensual perceptions in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: ye ca diṭṭhadhammikā rūpā, ye ca samparāyikā rūpā;
segs.e: visions in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: yā ca diṭṭhadhammikā rūpasaññā, yā ca samparāyikā rūpasaññā—
segs.e: perceptions of visions in this life and in lives to come;

segs.p: ubhayametaṁ aniccaṁ.
segs.e: all of these are impermanent.

segs.p: Yadaniccaṁ taṁ nālaṁ abhinandituṁ, nālaṁ abhivadituṁ, nālaṁ ajjhositun’ti.
segs.e: And what’s impermanent is not worth approving, welcoming, or clinging to.’

segs.p: Tassa evaṁpaṭipannassa tabbahulavihārino āyatane cittaṁ pasīdati.
segs.e: Practicing in this way and meditating on it often their mind becomes confident in this dimension.

segs.p: Sampasāde sati etarahi vā āneñjaṁ samāpajjati paññāya vā adhimuccati.
segs.e: Being confident, they either attain the imperturbable now, or are freed by wisdom.

segs.p: Kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā, ṭhānametaṁ vijjati yaṁ taṁsaṁvattanikaṁ viññāṇaṁ assa āneñjūpagaṁ.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, it’s possible that that conducive consciousness will be reborn in the imperturbable.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyā āneñjasappāyā paṭipadā akkhāyati.
segs.e: This is said to be the third way of practice suitable for attaining the imperturbable.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘ye ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmā, ye ca samparāyikā kāmā;
segs.e: ‘Sensual pleasures in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: yā ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmasaññā, yā ca samparāyikā kāmasaññā;
segs.e: sensual perceptions in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: ye ca diṭṭhadhammikā rūpā, ye ca samparāyikā rūpā;
segs.e: visions in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: yā ca diṭṭhadhammikā rūpasaññā, yā ca samparāyikā rūpasaññā;
segs.e: perceptions of visions in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: yā ca āneñjasaññā—
segs.e: and perceptions of the imperturbable;

segs.p: sabbā saññā.
segs.e: all are perceptions.

segs.p: Yatthetā aparisesā nirujjhanti etaṁ santaṁ etaṁ paṇītaṁ—
segs.e: Where they cease without remainder, that is peaceful, that is sublime,

segs.p: yadidaṁ ākiñcaññāyatanan’ti.
segs.e: namely the dimension of nothingness.’

segs.p: Tassa evaṁpaṭipannassa tabbahulavihārino āyatane cittaṁ pasīdati.
segs.e: Practicing in this way and meditating on it often their mind becomes confident in this dimension.

segs.p: Sampasāde sati etarahi vā ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samāpajjati paññāya vā adhimuccati.
segs.e: Being confident, they either attain the dimension of nothingness now, or are freed by wisdom.

segs.p: Kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā, ṭhānametaṁ vijjati yaṁ taṁsaṁvattanikaṁ viññāṇaṁ assa ākiñcaññāyatanūpagaṁ.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, it’s possible that that conducive consciousness will be reborn in the dimension of nothingness.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamā ākiñcaññāyatanasappāyā paṭipadā akkhāyati.
segs.e: This is said to be the first way of practice suitable for attaining the dimension of nothingness.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple has gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, and reflects like this:

segs.p: ‘suññamidaṁ attena vā attaniyena vā’ti.
segs.e: ‘This is empty of a self or what belongs to a self.’

segs.p: Tassa evaṁpaṭipannassa tabbahulavihārino āyatane cittaṁ pasīdati.
segs.e: Practicing in this way and meditating on it often their mind becomes confident in this dimension.

segs.p: Sampasāde sati etarahi vā ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samāpajjati paññāya vā adhimuccati.
segs.e: Being confident, they either attain the dimension of nothingness now, or are freed by wisdom.

segs.p: Kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā, ṭhānametaṁ vijjati yaṁ taṁsaṁvattanikaṁ viññāṇaṁ assa ākiñcaññāyatanūpagaṁ.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, it’s possible that that conducive consciousness will be reborn in the dimension of nothingness.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyā ākiñcaññāyatanasappāyā paṭipadā akkhāyati.
segs.e: This is said to be the second way of practice suitable for attaining the dimension of nothingness.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘nāhaṁ kvacani kassaci kiñcanatasmiṁ, na ca mama kvacani kismiñci kiñcanaṁ natthī’ti.
segs.e: ‘I don’t belong to anyone anywhere! And nothing belongs to me anywhere!’

segs.p: Tassa evaṁpaṭipannassa tabbahulavihārino āyatane cittaṁ pasīdati.
segs.e: Practicing in this way and meditating on it often their mind becomes confident in this dimension.

segs.p: Sampasāde sati etarahi vā ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samāpajjati paññāya vā adhimuccati.
segs.e: Being confident, they either attain the dimension of nothingness now, or are freed by wisdom.

segs.p: Kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā, ṭhānametaṁ vijjati yaṁ taṁsaṁvattanikaṁ viññāṇaṁ assa ākiñcaññāyatanūpagaṁ.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, it’s possible that that conducive consciousness will be reborn in the dimension of nothingness.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyā ākiñcaññāyatanasappāyā paṭipadā akkhāyati.
segs.e: This is said to be the third way of practice suitable for attaining the dimension of nothingness.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘ye ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmā, ye ca samparāyikā kāmā;
segs.e: ‘Sensual pleasures in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: yā ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmasaññā, yā ca samparāyikā kāmasaññā;
segs.e: sensual perceptions in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: ye ca diṭṭhadhammikā rūpā, ye ca samparāyikā rūpā;
segs.e: visions in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: yā ca diṭṭhadhammikā rūpasaññā, yā ca samparāyikā rūpasaññā;
segs.e: perceptions of visions in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: yā ca āneñjasaññā, yā ca ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā—
segs.e: perceptions of the imperturbable, and perceptions of the dimension of nothingness;

segs.p: sabbā saññā.
segs.e: all are perceptions.

segs.p: Yatthetā aparisesā nirujjhanti etaṁ santaṁ etaṁ paṇītaṁ—
segs.e: Where they cease without remainder, that is peaceful, that is sublime,

segs.p: yadidaṁ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanan’ti.
segs.e: namely the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.’

segs.p: Tassa evaṁpaṭipannassa tabbahulavihārino āyatane cittaṁ pasīdati.
segs.e: Practicing in this way and meditating on it often their mind becomes confident in this dimension.

segs.p: Sampasāde sati etarahi vā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samāpajjati paññāya vā adhimuccati.
segs.e: Being confident, they either attain the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception now, or are freed by wisdom.

segs.p: Kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā, ṭhānametaṁ vijjati yaṁ taṁsaṁvattanikaṁ viññāṇaṁ assa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagaṁ.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, it’s possible that that conducive consciousness will be reborn in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasappāyā paṭipadā akkhāyatī”ti.
segs.e: This is said to be the way of practice suitable for attaining the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “idha, bhante, bhikkhu evaṁ paṭipanno hoti:
segs.e: “Sir, take a mendicant who practices like this:

segs.p: ‘no cassa, no ca me siyā; na bhavissati, na me bhavissati; yadatthi yaṁ, bhūtaṁ—taṁ pajahāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘It might not be, and it might not be mine. It will not be, and it will not be mine. I am giving up what exists, what has come to be.’

segs.p: Evaṁ upekkhaṁ paṭilabhati.
segs.e: In this way they gain equanimity.

segs.p: Parinibbāyeyya nu kho so, bhante, bhikkhu na vā parinibbāyeyyā”ti?
segs.e: Would that mendicant become extinguished or not?”

segs.p: “Apetthekacco, ānanda, bhikkhu parinibbāyeyya, apetthekacco bhikkhu na parinibbāyeyyā”ti.
segs.e: “One such mendicant might become extinguished, Ānanda, while another might not.”

segs.p: “Ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo yenapetthekacco bhikkhu parinibbāyeyya, apetthekacco bhikkhu na parinibbāyeyyā”ti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason for this?”

segs.p: “Idhānanda, bhikkhu evaṁ paṭipanno hoti:
segs.e: “Ānanda, take a mendicant who practices like this:

segs.p: ‘no cassa, no ca me siyā; na bhavissati, na me bhavissati; yadatthi, yaṁ bhūtaṁ—taṁ pajahāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘It might not be, and it might not be mine. It will not be, and it will not be mine. I am giving up what exists, what has come to be.’

segs.p: Evaṁ upekkhaṁ paṭilabhati.
segs.e: In this way they gain equanimity.

segs.p: So taṁ upekkhaṁ abhinandati, abhivadati, ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: They approve, welcome, and keep clinging to that equanimity.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ upekkhaṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṁ hoti viññāṇaṁ tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: Their consciousness has that as support and fuel for grasping.

segs.p: Saupādāno, ānanda, bhikkhu na parinibbāyatī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with fuel for grasping does not become extinguished.”

segs.p: “Kahaṁ pana so, bhante, bhikkhu upādiyamāno upādiyatī”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, what is that mendicant grasping?”

segs.p: “Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ, ānandā”ti.
segs.e: “The dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.”

segs.p: “Upādānaseṭṭhaṁ kira so, bhante, bhikkhu upādiyamāno upādiyatī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, it seems that mendicant is grasping the best thing to grasp!”

segs.p: “Upādānaseṭṭhañhi so, ānanda, bhikkhu upādiyamāno upādiyati.
segs.e: “Indeed, Ānanda.

segs.p: Upādānaseṭṭhañhetaṁ, ānanda, yadidaṁ—
segs.e: For the best thing to grasp is

segs.p: nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ.
segs.e: the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: Idhānanda, bhikkhu evaṁ paṭipanno hoti:
segs.e: Take a mendicant who practices like this:

segs.p: ‘no cassa, no ca me siyā; na bhavissati, na me bhavissati; yadatthi, yaṁ bhūtaṁ—taṁ pajahāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘It might not be, and it might not be mine. It will not be, and it will not be mine. I am giving up what exists, what has come to be.’

segs.p: Evaṁ upekkhaṁ paṭilabhati.
segs.e: In this way they gain equanimity.

segs.p: So taṁ upekkhaṁ nābhinandati, nābhivadati, na ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: They don’t approve, welcome, or keep clinging to that equanimity.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ upekkhaṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato na tannissitaṁ hoti viññāṇaṁ na tadupādānaṁ.
segs.e: So their consciousness doesn’t have that as support and fuel for grasping.

segs.p: Anupādāno, ānanda, bhikkhu parinibbāyatī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant free of grasping becomes extinguished.”

segs.p: “Acchariyaṁ, bhante, abbhutaṁ, bhante.
segs.e: “It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing!

segs.p: Nissāya nissāya kira no, bhante, bhagavatā oghassa nittharaṇā akkhātā.
segs.e: It seems the Buddha has explained to us how to cross over the flood by relying on one support or another.

segs.p: Katamo pana, bhante, ariyo vimokkho”ti?
segs.e: But sir, what is noble liberation?”

segs.p: “Idhānanda, bhikkhu ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: “Ānanda, it’s when a noble disciple reflects like this:

segs.p: ‘ye ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmā, ye ca samparāyikā kāmā;
segs.e: ‘Sensual pleasures in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: yā ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmasaññā, yā ca samparāyikā kāmasaññā;
segs.e: sensual perceptions in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: ye ca diṭṭhadhammikā rūpā, ye ca samparāyikā rūpā;
segs.e: visions in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: yā ca diṭṭhadhammikā rūpasaññā, yā ca samparāyikā rūpasaññā;
segs.e: perceptions of visions in this life and in lives to come,

segs.p: yā ca āneñjasaññā, yā ca ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā, yā ca nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññā—
segs.e: perceptions of the imperturbable, perceptions of the dimension of nothingness, perceptions of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception;

segs.p: esa sakkāyo yāvatā sakkāyo.
segs.e: that is substantial reality as far as substantial reality extends.

segs.p: Etaṁ amataṁ yadidaṁ anupādā cittassa vimokkho.
segs.e: But this is freedom from death, namely the liberation of the mind by not grasping.’

segs.p: Iti, kho, ānanda, desitā mayā āneñjasappāyā paṭipadā, desitā ākiñcaññāyatanasappāyā paṭipadā, desitā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasappāyā paṭipadā, desitā nissāya nissāya oghassa nittharaṇā, desito ariyo vimokkho.
segs.e: So, Ānanda, I have taught the ways of practice suitable for attaining the imperturbable, the dimension of nothingness, and the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. I have taught how to cross the flood by relying on one support or another, and I have taught noble liberation.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho, ānanda, satthārā karaṇīyaṁ sāvakānaṁ hitesinā anukampakena anukampaṁ upādāya, kataṁ vo taṁ mayā.
segs.e: Out of sympathy, I’ve done what a teacher should do who wants what’s best for their disciples.

segs.p: Etāni, ānanda, rukkhamūlāni, etāni suññāgārāni. Jhāyathānanda, mā pamādattha, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha. Ayaṁ vo amhākaṁ anusāsanī’”ti.
segs.e: Here are these roots of trees, and here are these empty huts. Practice absorption, Ānanda! Don’t be negligent! Don’t regret it later! This is my instruction to you.”

segs.p: Idamavoca bhagavā.
segs.e: That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandīti.
segs.e: Satisfied, Venerable Ānanda approved what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Āneñjasappāyasuttaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ chaṭṭhaṁ.
